headline: SILVER GAINS 2.3× GOLD in One Session; Ratio Compresses to 58.7 as Iran Talks Lift Industrial Demand
snippet: Silver surged 2.99% on May 25 vs. gold's 1.31% gain as Iran peace deal optimism revived industrial demand expectations. The gold-silver ratio compressed to 58.7:1, below the post-2000 average of 60–65:1 — silver is now catching both a monetary bid and an industrial bid simultaneously. JP Morgan targets $81/oz average for full-year 2026; Citigroup sees $110 in H2 citing acute physical supply shortages.

headline: "MARGIN CALL FROM THE PHYSICAL WORLD" — Sovereign Gold Selloff Could Prime Metal's Next Bull Run, Says SPI's Innes
snippet: Gold pulled back to $4,489 on May 26, but SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes argues the recent wave of emergency sovereign liquidations — driven by energy-importing nations scrambling for dollar liquidity after the Hormuz closure — were tactical, not ideological. Innes sees the coming yield curve pivot as bullion's next major tailwind: central banks that marched reserves to the "pawn shop window" will buy them back.

headline: COPPER AT $6.20: China Acid Ban Strips 3M Tonnes from Market; Some Chilean Mines Below 30 Days of Inventory
snippet: China's effective May 1 ban on industrial sulfuric acid exports — a by-product of copper and zinc smelting — removes roughly 3 million tonnes from the global seaborne market. Chile, the world's largest copper producer and the biggest acid importer, sources 37.1% from China. Some SX-EW heap-leach operations are reportedly below 30 days of supply inventory. Copper futures sit at $6.20/lb after pulling back from the May 13 record of $6.65.

headline: ATHABASCA ASSAY: Cosa Resources Hits 1.7% U3O8 in 0.5m at Murphy Lake North, Denison Mines JV
snippet: Cosa Resources (TSXV: COSA) confirmed chemical assays showing 1.7% U3O8 over 0.5m within a broader 5.0m interval averaging 0.55% U3O8 at Murphy Lake North — a joint venture with Denison Mines located 3km east of IsoEnergy's Hurricane deposit in Saskatchewan's eastern Athabasca Basin. Mineralisation includes anomalous nickel and cobalt, consistent with sandstone-hosted Athabasca uranium deposits.

headline: NexGen LAUNCHES 29,200m Summer Drill at PCE; High-Grade Uranium Zone Expands 33% to 550m Vertical
snippet: NexGen Energy (NYSE/TSX: NXE) kicked off its 29,200-metre summer campaign at Patterson Corridor East (PCE) this week, following winter drilling that expanded the high-grade subdomain by 33% to 550m in vertical extent across a 210m strike. 79 of 115 total PCE holes intersected mineralisation; 21 returned off-scale radioactivity above 61,000 cps. Full 2026 program targets 42,000m.

headline: PORPHYRY CONFIRMED: Kobrea Phase 1 Defines Large Cu-Au-Mo System at El Perdido, Mendoza Province, Argentina
snippet: Kobrea Exploration (TSXV: KBX) completed 2,358 metres across six Phase 1 holes at El Perdido in Mendoza Province, confirming a large hydrothermal porphyry copper-gold-molybdenum system. Chalcocite enrichment was intersected in hole DD26ELP004; alteration intensity, veining, and sulphide grades strengthen at depth — and the core of the system remains untested.

headline: Sun Summit Fires Up RECORD $10M DRILL at B.C.'s Toodoggone Gold District; Maiden Resource Targeted Q1 2027
snippet: Sun Summit Minerals (TSXV: SMN) launched a fully funded 10,000-metre, $10 million drill program at the JD Project in B.C.'s Toodoggone Gold District, targeting the Creek-to-Finn corridor. Previous intercepts include 81.0m @ 4.80 g/t gold and 122.5m @ 2.11 g/t gold. A maiden NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate is targeted for Q1 2027.

headline: USAR: Inside America's First "Mine-to-Magnet" Rare Earth Play — Texas Deposit, Oklahoma Magnet Factory
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) aims to be the U.S.'s first vertically integrated rare earth company — mining the Round Top polymetallic deposit in West Texas and manufacturing permanent magnets at a facility in Oklahoma. The stock has surged in 2026 on supply-chain nationalism tailwinds. Analysts see significant strategic value but flag execution risk: no mine-to-magnet U.S. pipeline has been built at scale before.

headline: GDX UP ~50% YTD — GOLD MINERS Finally Outperforming Bullion; Operational Leverage Is the Thesis
snippet: The Gold Miners Index has returned roughly 50% year-to-date through April 2026, outpacing both physical gold and the broader equity market. At $4,400+ gold, operational leverage means every incremental dollar in the gold price drops almost entirely to miners' bottom lines. Precious metals miners are outpacing battery metals names — a split S&P Global described as gold's "banner year."

headline: LITHIUM DEMAND FLOOR Forming in Energy Storage; MinRes Reboots Bald Hill as Prices Recover Above 180,000 CNY/T
snippet: Stationary energy storage is emerging as lithium's structural demand floor even as passenger EV growth moderates. China pledged to double national EV charging capacity to 180 GW by 2027 and grid-scale battery deployments are absorbing projected surplus. Mineral Resources restarted its Bald Hill mine in Western Australia (165,000 dmt/yr capacity) and Core Lithium restarted Finniss following an 18-month price-driven shutdown.
